_about: Single source for the demo video narration: TTS (say), burned-in captions and the .srt (caption), SCRIPT.md (facts, rubric). 'say' may spell numbers for the voice; 'caption' is what is shown. Fact IDs refer to apps/web/src/content/sources.json; CH = the official challenge page (https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/nasas-discarded-equipment-storytelling/); DR = design reasoning (a team choice, not a factual claim); BUILD = verified in the current build (docs/DECISIONS.md inventory).

lines.say: In 1969, Apollo 11 landed on the Moon. Part of its lander is still up there today.
lines.caption: In 1969, Apollo 11 landed on the Moon. Part of its lander is still up there today.

lines.say: We're a team from the Philippines, and this is Space Archaeologist.
lines.caption: We're a team from the Philippines, and this is Space Archaeologist.

lines.say: Our challenge is called Abandoned but not Forgotten.
lines.caption: Our challenge is called Abandoned but not Forgotten.

lines.say: Since the 1960s, NASA has left machines on the Moon and on Mars.
lines.caption: Since the 1960s, NASA has left machines on the Moon and on Mars.

lines.say: A laser reflector that scientists still bounce light off today. A rover that drove more than a marathon on Mars.
lines.caption: A laser reflector that scientists still bounce light off today. A rover that drove more than a marathon on Mars.

lines.say: But the challenge notes that kids mostly hear about today's missions. The old machines live in dense websites and textbooks.
lines.caption: But the challenge notes that kids mostly hear about today's missions. The old machines live in dense websites and textbooks.

lines.say: We believe kids learn best by doing. So we asked: what if kids could dig these stories up themselves?
lines.caption: We believe kids learn best by doing. So we asked: what if kids could dig these stories up themselves?

lines.say: Space Archaeologist is a free browser game. Kids aged seven to twelve explore the real machines left on the Moon and Mars, and learn their true stories.
lines.caption: Space Archaeologist is a free browser game. Kids aged 7 to 12 explore the real machines left on the Moon and Mars, and learn their true stories.

lines.say: You design an explorer, board the ship, and pick a mission. Then come real NASA film, a launch, digs and games, and a badge at the end.
lines.caption: You design an explorer, board the ship, and pick a mission. Then come real NASA film, a launch, digs and games, and a badge at the end.

lines.say: And Nova, a friendly AI guide, answers questions the whole way.
lines.caption: And Nova, a friendly AI guide, answers questions the whole way.

lines.say: Here's the real game, recorded from the current build.
lines.caption: Here's the real game, recorded from the current build.

lines.say: Press start. Nova gives a short tour. Type a nickname, and design your explorer.
lines.caption: Press start. Nova gives a short tour. Type a nickname, and design your explorer.

lines.say: This is the ship. Two missions are ready to play.
lines.caption: This is the ship. Two missions are ready to play.

lines.say: Mission one opens with real Apollo 11 film from NASA.
lines.caption: Mission one opens with real Apollo 11 film from NASA.

lines.say: Then you pull the lever. The Saturn V lifts off, and you fly to the Moon.
lines.caption: Then you pull the lever. The Saturn V lifts off, and you fly to the Moon.

lines.say: On the Moon, the path at the top shows every step. Walk around, scan, and follow the glints.
lines.caption: On the Moon, the path at the top shows every step. Walk around, scan, and follow the glints.

lines.say: Every find starts with a dig. Brush the dust away.
lines.caption: Every find starts with a dig. Brush the dust away.

lines.say: Then turn it around, and open its glowing parts to see what each one does.
lines.caption: Then turn it around, and open its glowing parts to see what each one does.

lines.say: This is the laser reflector. Send a laser ping, and watch the light come back. Scientists still do this today.
lines.caption: This is the laser reflector. Send a laser ping, and watch the light come back. Scientists still do this today.

lines.say: Then comes a quick quiz. Hold up one, two, three or four fingers to answer A, B, C or D.
lines.caption: Then comes a quick quiz. Hold up one, two, three or four fingers to answer A, B, C or D.

lines.say: In the Rock Box, you catch Moon rocks with your own hands. Apollo 11 brought home about twenty one and a half kilograms.
lines.caption: In the Rock Box, you catch Moon rocks with your own hands. Apollo 11 brought home about 21.5 kilograms.

lines.say: Next, rebuild the lander, and put its journey back in order.
lines.caption: Next, rebuild the lander, and put its journey back in order.

lines.say: The mission report is a quiz nobody fails. A wrong answer just becomes a hint.
lines.caption: The mission report is a quiz nobody fails. A wrong answer just becomes a hint.

lines.say: Then you earn a badge, and the chapter is complete.
lines.caption: Then you earn a badge, and the chapter is complete.

lines.say: On Mars, you keep the rover Opportunity going. Wipe the dust off its solar panels, just like the real Martian wind did.
lines.caption: On Mars, you keep the rover Opportunity going. Wipe the dust off its solar panels, just like the real Martian wind did.

lines.say: And any time, kids can simply ask Nova, out loud.
lines.caption: And any time, kids can simply ask Nova, out loud.

lines.say: The game turns the question into text right on this computer. Then Nova checks her facts.
lines.caption: The game turns the question into text right on this computer. Then Nova checks her facts.

lines.say: Every feature is there for a reason.
lines.caption: Every feature is there for a reason.

lines.say: Kids ask lots of questions. Nova answers by voice or text, stays on space topics, and uses facts with real sources.
lines.caption: Kids ask lots of questions. Nova answers by voice or text, stays on space topics, and uses facts with real sources.

lines.say: Moving your real hands to scan, grab and ping makes learning active. And it's optional. Mouse, keyboard and touch work everywhere.
lines.caption: Moving your real hands to scan, grab and ping makes learning active. And it's optional. Mouse, keyboard and touch work everywhere.

lines.say: And every story is read aloud, with captions, so younger kids and early readers can follow along.
lines.caption: And every story is read aloud, with captions, so younger kids and early readers can follow along.

lines.say: It's all built on NASA data. Two hundred seventy five facts, each linked to one of forty six NASA sources, and checked by our fact tests.
lines.caption: It's all built on NASA data. 275 facts, each linked to one of 46 NASA sources, and checked by our fact tests.

lines.say: Nova can even check live NASA feeds: asteroids passing Earth today, space weather, and the weather on Mars.
lines.caption: Nova can even check live NASA feeds: asteroids passing Earth today, space weather, and the weather on Mars.

lines.say: It's built for kids' safety. No accounts. Camera and voice are processed on the computer. And grown-ups can switch the AI off.
lines.caption: It's built for kids' safety. No accounts. Camera and voice are processed on the computer. And grown-ups can switch the AI off.

lines.say: Captions are always on. There's calm motion, an easy-read font, and no camera needed. Even offline, Nova answers from the game's own fact sheet.
lines.caption: Captions are always on. There's calm motion, an easy-read font, and no camera needed. Even offline, Nova answers from the game's own fact sheet.

lines.say: Space Archaeologist is free, and it runs in a web browser. No downloads, and no accounts.
lines.caption: Space Archaeologist is free, and it runs in a web browser. No downloads, and no accounts.

lines.say: It's designed so a seven year old can finish it, and older kids still chase three stars.
lines.caption: It's designed so a 7-year-old can finish it, and older kids still chase three stars.

lines.say: Our goal: every kid walks away knowing what was left behind, why it stayed, and that scientists still use it.
lines.caption: Our goal: every kid walks away knowing what was left behind, why it stayed, and that scientists still use it.

lines.say: Three more missions are planned: Viking 1, Pioneer 10, and Voyager 1.
lines.caption: Three more missions are planned: Viking 1, Pioneer 10, and Voyager 1.

lines.say: Space Archaeologist turns the machines NASA left behind into a game kids can play, so their stories are never forgotten.
lines.caption: Space Archaeologist turns the machines NASA left behind into a game kids can play, so their stories are never forgotten.

lines.say: Play it free, right now, in your browser.
lines.caption: Play it free, right now, in your browser.

kid.say: Nova, how far away is the Moon?
kid.caption: Nova, how far away is the Moon?
kid.note: A player's question voiced by a neutral adult text-to-speech voice for this recording (Space Apps rules: no voices or likenesses of anyone under 18). Labelled on screen; the game's real speech-to-text hears it.
